title: Canonical exceptional and dualizing base-change arrows
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring of universe $u+1$. For schemes $X,S,S'$ of universe $u$ [def-pc-scheme], work in ordinary etale derived module categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $f:X\to S$ be quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with chosen compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], let $g:S'\to S$, and form $X'=X\times_SS'$ with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$ [def-pc-base-change]. Write $P_f=Rf_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and $P_f\dashv G_f=f^\times$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], with counit $\varepsilon_f$, and likewise for $f'$. Inverse images mean the exact constant-coefficient inverse image extended to the derived category [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Define $\beta_{f,g,K}:g'^*G_fK\to G_{f'}g^*K$ as the transpose of the inverse compact-support base-change comparison $P_{f'}g'^*G_fK\to g^*P_fG_fK$, followed by $g^*\varepsilon_f(K)$. Define the dualizing base-change map $g'^*\omega_f\to\omega_{f'}$, where $\omega_f=G_fA_S$, as $\beta_{f,g,A_S}$ followed by $G_{f'}$ of the canonical inverse-image unit identification $g^*A_S\simeq A_{S'}$. These definitions assert no smoothness or invertibility conclusion.
